summary: How should the accountable owner resolve the remaining reconciliation responsibility: keep package working-title labeling with the delivery owner, revise the baseline implementation brief, and decide whether to obtain implementation/full-juice integration capacity or change the power-up catch juice deliverable?

options.label: Name the delivery owner for package labeling, revise the baseline brief, and defer power-up catch ownership pending capacity
options.description:
This resolves the clearly assignable package-label responsibility and corrects the baseline brief without changing scope. It leaves the power-up catch juice ownership gap and implementation capacity unresolved, so execution and evidence for that deliverable remain blocked.
Next work: Assign package working-title acceptance to the delivery owner and create a checklist verifying that the internal build package and run instructions use the approved working title without final branding claims. Revise the baseline increment to include clean-checkout setup, reproducible dependencies, committed lockfile, development command, passive frame-time observation hook, and power-up catch integration dependency. Update the ownership map with the unresolved power-up catch owner.

options.label: Request a bounded implementation/full-juice integration capacity decision while continuing non-implementation preparation
options.description:
This keeps accepted scope intact and records that the blocker is capacity/ownership, not an accepted scope change. It requires the accountable owner to choose whether authorized staffing, existing capacity, budget/time authority, or another resourcing path is available; it does not assume a hire, purchase, contract, or waiver. Implementation remains blocked until that decision is made.
Next work: Produce a bounded capacity proposal with required capabilities: clean-checkout setup, committed lockfile, one-layout core slice, package working-title build label, and distinct power-up catch juice integration. State dependencies, risks, assumptions, and evidence. Reconcile package-label ownership under the delivery owner unless a technical packaging owner is explicitly assigned. Continue brief revision and non-engineering prep.

options.label: Change the accepted juice pass so power-up catch feedback is only covered generically
options.description:
This would reduce implementation and evidence burden but conflicts with accepted deliverable expectations and weakens first-time-player and audio-led feel evidence. It changes product assurance coverage and requires Director approval; it should not be treated as a planning shortcut.
Next work: Prepare a Director-facing scope/risk trade showing the removed distinct catch-feedback treatment, impact on power-up readability, peak-load/accessibility evidence, and first-time-player acceptance criteria. Do not change implementation or test plans until approved.

options.label: Pause reconciliation to investigate existing qualified implementation, full-juice, VFX-audio, or packaging owners before requesting capacity
options.description:
This is useful only if current resource evidence is incomplete. If investigation confirms only oversight/planning roles and empty implementation resources, it adds delay while leaving the capacity gap unchanged.
Next work: Inspect authorized resource records and current commitments for any assigned or contractually available owner capable of implementation/full-juice integration and package label verification, excluding oversight-only roles. If found, name the owner, define the acceptance outcome, and repair the brief. If absent, record the evidence and move to the bounded capacity decision.

options.label: Give different direction
options.description: Describe your intended outcome; the responsible agent will assess the next authorized work.

question: Reconcile the remaining responsibility: The approved full juice and particle feedback pass must include a distinct treatment for power-up catch.. Affected work: Power-Up Interaction Payoffs, Full Juice and Adaptive Audio, First-Time Player Acceptance and Hypothesis Evidence. Accountable: Marcus Vale. No user decision is requested. Review retained specialist advice within delegated authority: powerUpCatchFeedback: missingResponsibility: Add a named owner and explicit outcome for the concrete power-up catch juice event treatment, distinct from generic juice pass ownership and distinct from each power-up static visual/audio identity. suggestedOwner: The existing full-juice/VFX-audio integration owner should own the catch event treatment, with gameplay confirmation that the cue fires on successful power-up catch and does not obscure ball, paddle, power-up, or critical gameplay readability. proposedAcceptanceOutcome: For each approved power-up, the build demonstrates a catch-triggered feedback moment tied to the full juice and particle pass, consistent with the required event list and readable within the existing peak-load and accessibility constraints. sourcePreserved: Accepted deliverables require the full juice and particle feedback pass to be tied to launch, paddle hit, brick hit, brick clear, power-up catch, multiplier rise, layout clear, and failure/reset. Accepted acceptance criteria require a first-time player to catch power-ups and require five power-ups each to have distinct behavior, readable visual identity, and identifiable audio cue, while peak spectacle must not obscure ball, paddle, critical brick states, or power-ups. packageWorkingTitle: missingResponsibility: Add a named owner and explicit delivery check ensuring the Chromium ZIP/local build package and its run instructions are labeled with the approved working title, Prism Break PoC. suggestedOwner: The Producer/Delivery owner should own package and documentation labeling, with technical packaging review by the Technical Director if packaging readiness is assigned to technical ownership. If no Technical Director ownership is evidenced for packaging, the Producer-led feasibility and packaging path remains the source-preserving owner. proposedAcceptanceOutcome: The delivered local build package and run instructions visibly and consistently identify Prism Break PoC as the internal working title, without introducing final title, branding, or trademark claims before separate external clearance review. sourcePreserved: Accepted constraints state that Prism Break is acceptable as an internal PoC working placeholder title, that the Prism Break PoC working title should be used in packages, and that final title, branding, and trademark clearance are separate before external release or brand-facing use. Accepted acceptance criteria and deliverables require a Chromium-compatible ZIP/local build with run instructions and source project files and asset sources where applicable. authorityBoundary: This is advisory reconciliation and proposed ownership coverage. It does not change authority, approve scope, require a new release, or treat a hypothetical failure as an observed condition.

reply.rationale: Keep the accepted scope intact: the package and run instructions must use the approved internal working title Prism Break PoC, with the Producer/Delivery owner owning label acceptance unless a technical packaging owner is explicitly assigned. Revise the baseline implementation brief now to require clean-checkout setup, committed lockfile, development command, passive frame-time observation hook, and explicit power-up catch integration dependency. The remaining blocker is not scope; it is a named implementation/full-juice integration owner and capacity. Prepare a bounded capacity proposal for the distinct power-up catch juice treatment and baseline engineering capabilities, continue non-implementation preparation, and do not generalize or change the accepted power-up catch juice deliverable without a Director-approved scope/risk trade.
